newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PHILADELPHIA'S LEGION OF DOOM LINE GUNS DOWN SENATORS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PHILADELPHIA'S LEGION OF DOOM LINE GUNS DOWN SENATORS.

text.p: John LeClair scored a hat trick and Eric Lindros had a goal and five assists to lead the Philadelphia Flyers to a wild 8-5 victory over the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday.

Philadelphia's "Legion of Doom" line combined for 15 points in out-gunning the Senators. Mikael Renberg had two goals and three assists, LeClair added an assist to his three-goal performance, while Lindros' six-point night matched a career-high.
"It was a great night," LeClair said. "Actually, Renberg had great vision tonight, the best I've ever seen from him."

LeClair, who reached the 40-goal plateau by completing his hat trick with 51 seconds left in regulation, scored twice in an eight-goal first period that saw the score tied 4-4 at the first intermission.

Paul Coffey and Rod Brind'Amour also scored for the Flyers. Brind'Amour's power-play goal with 51 seconds left in the second period broke a 5-5 tie as the Flyers scored four unanswered goals after falling behind 5-4.
Shawn McEachern had a goal and two assists in the first period for Ottawa.
"For two periods we stayed with them," Ottawa coach Jacques Martin said. "The difference tonight was obviously the Lindros line. They scored all the goals and did all the damage."

On Long Island, the newest Devils made an immediate impact as Doug Gilmour contributed a goal and three assists and Dave Ellett added two assists in New Jersey's 5-3 victory over the New York Islanders.
New Jersey, which acquired Gilmour and Ellett Tuesday in a five-player trade with Toronto, moved past idle Florida into second place in the Atlantic Division with 72 points.
The Devils blew a 3-0 first-period lead by surrendering three goals in the second.
But Gilmour set up Lyle Odelein with the game-winner at 11:05 of the third period and added an insurance goal on a power play with 1:10 left in the third period.
"I was nervous and excited. You'd think guys our age wouldn't be nervous," said the 33-year-old Gilmour.
In Hartford, Ethan Moreau scored early in the third period and Chris Terreri made 32 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks rallied for a 2-2 tie with the Whalers.
Moreau took a pass from Murray Craven and broke around defenceman Glen Featherstone before sliding a backhander under goaltender Sean Burke 1:51 into the second period.
Alexei Zhamnov scored the first Chicago goal in the second period after Jeff O'Neill and Kent Manderville scored in the first to stake Hartford to a 2-0 lead.
In Toronto, Dale Hunter had a goal and an assist and Jim Carey made 28 saves as the Washington Capitals skated to a 3-1 victory over the Maple Leafs.
Calle Johansson, who scored on Washington's first shot of the game 4:51 into the contest, and Craig Berube notched the other goals for the Capitals.
Wendel Clark scored Toronto's lone goal with an assist from Steve Sullivan, who came from New Jersey in the trade that sent Maple Leafs captain Doug Gilmour to the Devils.
In Calgary, Craig Janney had two goals and an assist and Mike Gartner added a pair of tallies 2:30 apart in a four-goal first period as the Phoenix Coyotes beat the Flames 5-2.
Janney got the Coyotes on the scoreboard just 29 seconds into the game by re-directing Oleg Tverdovsky's slap shot between the pads of Calgary goaltender Trevor Kidd.
Jeremy Roenick scored the other Phoenix goal, a short-handed tally that snapped a 1-1 first-period tie.
Phoenix goalie Nikolai Khabibulin made 30 stops as the Coyotes improved to 17-0-1 when scoring first this season.
In Anaheim, Joe Sacco set up third-period goals by Bobby Dollas and Sean Pronger that lifted the Mighty Ducks into a 3-3 tie with the Edmonton Oilers.
Sacco had the puck behind the Edmonton net and passed to Pronger, who flipped a wrist shot over goaltender Curtis Joseph's glove with 2:44 left to knot the score.
Second period powerplay goals by Mike Grier and Mariusz Czerkawski had put Edmonton in front 3-1.
Joseph made 34 saves for the Oilers, while Anaheim goalie Guy Hebert turned aside 31 shots, including six in overtime.
